speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the rash first appeared and whether it is raised or flat?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression of symptoms, particularly the facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a body rash, is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum. Has the facial rash had a "slapped cheek" appearance, and are there any joint pains or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
